concepts.title: Isotope Mixtures and Average Atomic Mass
concepts.definition: One atomic mass unit is a twelfth of a neutral carbon-12 atom's mass, about 1.6605e-27 kg. Because most elements occur as a blend of isotopes, the listed atomic mass is the abundance-weighted mean of the isotope masses, which is why chlorine lands near 35.5 u instead of a whole number.
concepts.key_idea: Non-integer atomic masses signal an isotope mixture, not a measurement error.

concepts.title: Nuclide Composition: Protons, Neutrons, Mass Number
concepts.definition: A nuclide is labelled with its proton count Z and mass number A, the total of protons plus neutrons. Species sharing Z but not N are isotopes, those sharing A are isobars, and those sharing N are isotones.
concepts.key_idea: Chemical behaviour follows Z alone, which is why isotopes sit in one periodic-table slot.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph205.txt section 13.2 (Z, N, A notation, isotope/isobar/isotone examples like H-3 and He-3)

concepts.title: Nuclear Radius From Mass Number
concepts.definition: Fast-electron scattering shows that a nucleus of mass number A has radius R equal to 1.2 femtometre times the cube root of A. Bigger nuclei pack in more nucleons without growing much in radius.
concepts.key_idea: Because R goes as the cube root of A, radius ratios come from cube roots of mass-number ratios.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph205.txt section 13.3 (R = R0 A^(1/3), R0 = 1.2 fm, Exercise 13.4)

concepts.title: Nuclear Density Is a Universal Constant
concepts.definition: Since volume grows in step with A while mass does too, every nucleus has roughly the same density, near 2.3e17 kg per cubic metre -- about a hundred trillion times denser than water and comparable to neutron-star matter.
concepts.key_idea: Constant nuclear density means nuclei behave like incompressible liquid drops.

concepts.title: Mass-Energy Equivalence
concepts.definition: Relativity treats mass as a stored form of energy: a mass m carries an equivalent energy of m times the square of the speed of light. Converting even one gram of matter completely to energy releases about 9e13 joule.
concepts.key_idea: The factor c squared is enormous, so tiny masses correspond to huge energies.

concepts.title: Mass Defect and Nuclear Binding Energy
concepts.definition: A bound nucleus weighs less than its separate protons and neutrons. That shortfall, the mass defect, converts into the binding energy through 1 u = 931.5 MeV, the energy you must supply to pull the nucleus completely apart.
concepts.key_idea: Hydrogen-atom and neutron masses let atomic masses be used directly since electron masses cancel.

solution_steps.explain: Z hydrogen-atom masses plus A - Z neutron masses; electrons cancel against the atomic mass
the difference is the mass defect in atomic mass units

concepts.title: Binding Energy Per Nucleon
concepts.definition: Dividing a nucleus's total binding energy by its nucleon count gives the average energy that holds one nucleon in, the standard yardstick for how tightly different nuclei are bound.
concepts.key_idea: Stability tracks Ebn, not total binding energy: mid-mass nuclei top the table near 8.75 MeV.

concepts.title: Reading the Binding Energy Curve
concepts.definition: The plot of binding energy per nucleon against mass number rises steeply for light nuclei, stays near 8 MeV from A about 30 to 170, peaks at 8.75 MeV for A = 56, then sags for the heaviest nuclei. Both fission and fusion pay out because products move up this curve.
concepts.key_idea: Energy is released by any change, splitting heavy or merging light, that climbs toward the curve's flat summit.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph205.txt section 13.4.2 conclusions (i)-(iv) and section 13.7 opening

solution_steps.explain: steep climb below A = 30, plateau near 8 MeV across 30 to 170, slow fall beyond

concepts.title: Properties of the Nuclear Force
concepts.definition: The strong attraction gluing nucleons beats the Coulomb repulsion between protons, cuts off beyond a few femtometres, and treats protons and neutrons alike -- it is charge blind. Its potential well bottoms out near 0.8 fm, repulsive below that and attractive beyond.
concepts.formula: nuclear force: strongest known, short range near a few fm, charge independent
concepts.key_idea: Short range explains saturation, hence the constancy of binding energy per nucleon in mid-mass nuclei.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph205.txt section 13.5 (three listed properties, Fig. 13.2 potential minimum at 0.8 fm)

solution_steps.explain: nuclear attraction beats Coulomb repulsion between protons; gravity is negligible

proton-proton, neutron-proton and neutron-neutron attractions are nearly identical

concepts.title: Three Modes of Radioactive Decay
concepts.definition: An unstable nucleus sheds excess energy by emitting an alpha particle (a helium-4 nucleus), a beta particle (an electron or positron), or gamma photons of high energy. Becquerel's fogged photographic plate was the first clue that some nuclei decay spontaneously.
concepts.formula: alpha decay = he-4 out; beta decay = electron or positron out; gamma decay = photon out
concepts.key_idea: Radioactivity originates in the nucleus, not in the electron shells, and changes one nuclide into another.
question_patterns: name the three types of radioactive decay and what each emits

solution_steps.explain: alpha is a helium-4 nucleus, beta is an electron or positron, gamma is a high-energy photon
alpha and beta transmute the nucleus into a different element; gamma only lowers excitation
all three arise from the nucleus itself, which is why shielding and chemistry do not stop them

concepts.title: Q Value and Energy Balance
concepts.definition: The Q value of a reaction is the kinetic energy gained, equal to the initial minus the final rest mass expressed in energy. A positive Q marks an exothermic reaction, a negative Q an endothermic one that needs imported energy.
concepts.key_idea: Nucleon counts stay balanced across any nuclear equation; the mass difference alone decides Q.

solution_steps.explain: add the reactant masses and subtract the product masses, all in atomic mass units
multiply by 931.5; a positive result means the reaction liberates energy

concepts.title: Fission Energy From Fuel Mass
concepts.definition: In fission a heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 absorbs a neutron and splits into two mid-weight fragments plus spare neutrons, releasing about 200 MeV each time. Counting the atoms in a fuel sample turns that per-fission figure into a total energy yield.
concepts.key_idea: Roughly 10^14 joule per kilogram makes fission a million-fold richer than burning coal.

concepts.title: Thermonuclear Fusion in Stars
concepts.definition: Light nuclei fuse once they punch through the Coulomb barrier, roughly 400 keV for two protons, which demands temperatures near 10^9 kelvin -- thermonuclear fusion. Inside the sun the proton-proton cycle burns four hydrogens into one helium, paying out 26.7 MeV.
concepts.key_idea: Fusion needs crushing temperature to beat electrostatic repulsion, yet the sun gets by with high-energy protons from its distribution.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph205.txt section 13.7.2 (Eqs. 13.13-13.15, barrier ~400 keV, T ~ 3e9 K, sun core 1.5e7 K)
